comparator.name: Linguistics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formal 2026–2027 regulations list 180 EC for September 2026 entrants, with a 30 EC minor and three of five 10 EC portfolio seminars. The published seminar prerequisites still use older course names. The credit structure is supported, while entry to two of the illustrated seminars remains to be confirmed for this cohort.

exception.reason: Groningen’s September 2026 Linguistics curriculum lists the Psycholinguistics Project and three graduation seminars. The published entry rules for the Neurolinguistics and developmental-language-disorders seminars still name earlier courses. The equivalent requirements for the redesigned curriculum are not yet confirmed.
exception.curriculumContext: Articles 4.1 and 5.1(a) support 180 listed credits, including the open minor and three of five seminars. The dated Clinical Linguistics entry explicitly resolves the new cohort prerequisite from 2027–2028. Article 7.1 and the current portfolio course entries do not supply a reconciled entry rule for the new cohort’s two selected neuro- and psycholinguistics seminars.

audience.programmeDescription: Linguistics at the University of Groningen studies how people learn and use language, how languages are structured, and what happens when language is affected by a disorder.

curriculum.limitation: The listed courses account for 180 EC. Entry requirements for two graduation seminars have yet to be confirmed for students starting in September 2026.
